taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full taxonomy 0.6.7 review retains unclassified status. FC-000037 Control Availability Determination requires an uncertainty about a defined governance control’s availability before a material decision, not merely degraded service. FC-000048 Verification-Dependency Access Continuity requires a particular verifier blocked without a proportionate access transition. FC-000044 Primary Evidence Accessibility requires a specified authoritative artefact and authorised review question. None of these occurrence conditions is shown by the generic service notice. The case is an operational outage with taxonomy membership unresolved.

assessment_boundaries: This metadata pass does not retroactively claim direct inspection of every historical primary source.
Incident admission does not determine legal liability or establish every disputed claim as final fact.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI’s official incident page identifies the affected FedRAMP component, elevated errors beginning on 15 June and full recovery on 26 June. The independent status mirror corroborates the approximate duration. The notices do not identify the root cause, the fraction of requests affected, an unavailable governance control or the impact on a specific consequential review or customer. Degraded performance alone does not establish a compliance breach or data compromise.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: This is a documented prolonged availability incident in a FedRAMP service lane. The preserved record supports operational disruption, but it does not diagnose a distinct VIGIL failure mechanism involving authority, verification, oversight or control-state handling. Treating the FedRAMP label alone as proof of a governance-control failure would exceed the evidence.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: A prolonged degradation in an assured AI deployment lane matters for continuity planning and the ability of users to depend on an identified service tier. The status page describes availability; stronger governance claims would require evidence about which protected function, control or decision pathway was impaired.
